title: Protocol for analyzing and visualizing antiviral immune responses after acute infection of the murine oral mucosa
protocol: Reconstitute VACV inoculum by thawing a 1 mL vial on ice.
Sonicate the reconstituted virus for 45 seconds at 70% power.
Transport the virus to the vivarium on ice.
Anesthetize mice with an approved inhaled or injectable anesthetic.
Place a small drop of virus (∼10 μL) inside the lower lip (labial mucosa).
Gently poke the labial mucosa with a bifurcated needle.
Alternatively, dip the bifurcated needle into the virus stock.
Hold the virus between the prongs of the needle and gently poke it into the labial mucosa.
Wipe the inner lip with sterile gauze to remove any remaining VACV.
Monitor mice until they recover fully from anesthesia.
Prepare collection tubes for each sample.
Label screw cap 2 mL conical-bottom Sarstedt tube appropriately for each sample.
Thaw a 1 mL collagenase P aliquot in a 37°C water bath.
Add thawed collagenase P to 9 mL of RPMI medium.
Pipette 1 mL of diluted collagenase P (final concentration of 1 mg/mL) into each 2 mL tube.
Euthanize mice at the desired day post infection.
Remove the lower lip using dissection scissors and forceps, placing it in a 2 mL tube with diluted collagenase P.
Finely chop the dissected lips with scissors in diluted collagenase P.
Place the chopped tissue in a 37°C water bath for 45 minutes.
Vigorously pipette up and down with a 1000 μL pipette until the sample appears fully digested and homogenous.
Begin tissue processing immediately after sample collection.
Keep collected samples on ice until processing begins.
Establish ideal digestion parameters for each experiment.
Digest labial mucosal samples using collagenase I (10000 units/mL) for 45 minutes at 37°C.
Filter digested sample through a 70 μm cell strainer into a 5 mL tube.
Rinse filter with 3 additional milliliters of RPMI medium.
Centrifuge cells at 870 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 250 μL of RPMI medium.
Filter through a 60 μm 96-well filter plate.
Transfer filtered samples to a labeled 96-well round-bottom plate.
Centrifuge cells at 870 × g at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 250 μL of RPMI medium.
Count cells using Trypan Blue exclusion method.
Centrifuge cells at approximately 870 × g at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in diluted antibody solution.
Prepare antibody dilutions in HBSS + 0.1% BSA or compatible buffer.
A fixable viability dye can be included if necessary.
Protect samples from light and incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Add 200 μL of cold PBS to each well.
Centrifuge at approximately 870 × g at 4°C for 2 minutes.
Prepare 3.2% PFA by diluting 1:5 with PBS from a 16% PFA stock.
Discard supernatant and add 100 μL/sample of 3.2% PFA.
Pipette each sample to ensure resuspension.
Protect samples from light and incubate for 15 min at RT.
Centrifuge samples at ∼870 × g at 4°C for 2 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend in 250 μL of HBSS + 0.1% BSA + 0.1% EDTA.
Analyze via flow cytometry.
Plate 7.5 × 10^5 143B cells/well into 6-well plates.
Incubate cells overnight at 37°C with 9% CO2.
Freeze-thaw digested samples three times.
Prepare 6 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and label as 10−1, 10−2, 10−3, 10−4, 10−5, 10−6.
Add 1080 μL infection medium to each tube.
Add 120 μL of digested sample from 1 mL vial to 10−1 tube and mix well by pipetting.
Transfer 120 μL of 10−1 to 10−2 and mix well by pipetting.
Continue to dilute 1:10 from 10−2 to 10−6.
Prepare mouse for intravital microscopy.
Collect mouse from vivarium at desired time post-infection.
Place animal in induction chamber and induce anesthesia using 2% isoflurane.
Sterilize outer lip by alternating scrubs of Betadine and 70% ethanol.
Make two small incisions (approximately 2 mm) at the angles of the mouth using dissecting scissors.
Gently pull the lip through a mini-stage using tweezers.
Attach lip to the mini-stage using Vetbond or cyanoacrylate adhesive.
Place water-based lubricating gel on inner lip.
Turn mouse so that the lip makes stable, firm contact with a glass cover slip.
Tape both sides of the mini-stage firmly to the microscope stage to prevent movement and ensure contact with the coverslip.
Gently attach a nosecone to the mouse with surgical tape so as not to disturb the lip/mini-stage.
Secure nosecone and tubing to microscope stage using surgical tape.
Maintain anesthesia at a concentration of 1.75% or as otherwise determined.
Place the prepared mouse on the microscope in the heated environmental chamber.
Image the labial mucosal immune response using intravital microscopy.
Use a Leica DMi8 inverted five-channel confocal microscope equipped with an environmental chamber and dual multiphoton lasers for imaging.
Utilize ultrasensitive hybrid detectors and a 25 X water-immersion objective during imaging.
Maintain continuous, steady heat throughout the experiment.
Determine the lamina propria versus the mucosal epithelium using second harmonic generation of collagen signals.
Ensure an appropriate amount of water-based lubricant is applied to prevent the lip from drying.
